extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers for Research Project Grants (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and guidance for reviewers assessing Research Project Grant (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34) applications, including standard review criteria, program-specific considerations, and additional review topics (human subjects, animals, biohazards, resource sharing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution to the research field(s) involved, to provide research opportunities to students, and to strengthen the research environment of the institution, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion. Accordingly, reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach to the problem. Appropriate justification for the proposed work can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or from investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly in applications proposing pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of the R15 program: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 application; however, they may be included if available. Reviewers should also consider whether funding would substantially strengthen the research environment and expose students to research; whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience supervising students; and availability/likelihood of student participation and pursuit of biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 exploratory/developmental grant supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies that have the potential for significant impact on biomedical or biobehavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 need not have extensive background material or preliminary information. Reviewers will focus evaluation on the conceptual framework, the level of innovation, and the potential to significantly advance knowledge or understanding. Appropriate justification can be provided via literature citations, other data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required but may be included when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program (R34) supports development of Phase III clinical trials, including team establishment, tools for data management and oversight, recruitment strategies, finalization of protocol, and preparation of operations/procedures manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clinical Trial Planning Grant is not designed for collection of preliminary data or conduct of pilot studies to support the rationale for a clinical trial. Accordingly, reviewers will focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15, also consider whether the AREA award will have a substantial effect on the school/academic component in terms of strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or New Investigators, or in early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If collaborative or multi-PD/PI, do investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are leadership approach, governance and organizational structure appropriate? For R15, also assess whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project is in early stages, will the strategy establish feasibility and will particularly risky aspects be managed? If the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, are plans to address protection of human subjects from research risks and inclusion/exclusion (sex/gender, race, ethnicity, children) justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy? For R15, also consider whether the application provides sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest toward research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate for the project proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements? For R15, also evaluate availability of well-qualified students and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not meet exemption, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research that meets exemption categories, evaluate: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. See Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as inclusion (or exclusion) of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if inclusion/exclusion is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed. See Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points: (1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; (2) justifications for the use of animals and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers proposed; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research including the use of analgesic, anesthetic, and tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. See Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If needed, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision application relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval, the committee will consider whether the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether such opportunities either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application regarding Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) the procedures that will be used to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing certain types of resources, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of resource sharing specifically noted: (1) Data Sharing Plan; (2) Sharing Model Organisms; and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS). Reviewers comment on reasonableness of plans or rationale for not sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
